perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He works as a construction worker at a construction company where Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist; they are friendly but professional colleagues who interact during paperwork and project updates.
- Recently, he observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him. He suspected he might have upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknowing mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, not at all; she was dealing with personal stuff, and she apologized if she seemed short.
- After learning this, he felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He offered to listen and suggested a coffee break. He heard her accept and thank him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses, which Keith perceived as severe. He thanked her for sharing and suggested she consider talking to a professional. He heard her say she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- After suggesting professional help, he noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He believed he might have embarrassed her and felt regretful. He told her he hoped he had not overstepped and that he was there to support her. She replied that he hadn’t overstepped, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, he perceived Elizabeth as more open and appreciative of his concern. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He intended to maintain a supportive relationship. He told her he was glad they talked and that he was always available to chat or take a break. She thanked him, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
